of India |date=31 May 2011}} The company sells products related to [[List of art media|art materials]], [[writing implement]]s and office goods. == History == Camlin was established in 1931 by [[D. P. Dandekar]] and his brother G. P. Dandekar{{cite book |title=Limca Book of Records |date=2001 |publisher=Bisleri Beverages Limited |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y-JtAAAAMAAJ&q=Digambar+Dandekar |access-date=29 January 2022 |language=en}} starting operations as "Dandekar & Co." with "Horse Brand" Ink powders and tablets in 1931,{{cite web |title=About Kokuyo Camlin |url=https://www.kokuyocamlin.com/joint-venture/ |access-date=30 March 2024 |archive-date=30 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240330164326/https://www.kokuyocamlin.com/joint-venture/}} and shortly started producing "Camel ink" for fountain pens. It was incorporated as a [[privately held company|private company]] in 1946, and then turned into a [[public limited company]] in 1998. In 2011, [[Japan]]ese stationery major, "Kokuyo Co. Ltd", acquired a 50.74% stake in Camlin{{cite web |title= Kokuyo completes buyout of 51% in Camlin |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/kokuyo-completes-buyout-of-51-in-camlin-111102000170_1.html |access-date=31 March 2024|archive-date=31 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240331143903/https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/kokuyo-completes-buyout-of-51-in-camlin-111102000170_1.html |work=Business Standard|date=20 Jan 2013}} for {{INR}}366 [[crore]]. Dilip Dandekar continued as chairman and managing director of the company. The deal facilitated the entry of Kokuyo products, mainly paper and office stationery into the Indian market, while Camlin aimed to increase its exports to other countries.{{cite web |title= Japan's Kokuyo to buy majority stake in Camlin|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/japan-s-kokuyo-to-buy-majority-stake-in-camlin-111050200075_1.html |access-date=30 March 2024|archive-date=30 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240330152242/https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/japan-s-kokuyo-to-buy-majority-stake-in-camlin-111050200075_1.html |work=Business Standard|date=20 Jan 2013}} ==Kokuyo Japan== {{nihongo|'''Kokuyo Co., Ltd.'''|コクヨ株式会社|Kokuyo Kabushiki Gaisha}} is a Japanese [[manufacturing company]] of [[stationery]], office furniture, and office equipment. Kokuyo was established in Japan, in 1905 by Zentaro Kuroda, as "Kuroda Ledger Cover Shop" that made covers for Japanese-style account ledgers (wacho).{{cite web |title=About Kokuyo - Initiatives and History |url=https://www.kokuyo.com/about/initiatives-and-history/ |access-date=31 March 2024 |archive-date=3 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240303191412/https://www.kokuyo.com/about/initiatives-and-history/}} In 1914, the company name changed to Kuroda Kokkodo, and the manufacture of accounting slips, invoices, duplicate copybooks, and letter paper began. The company began using the current name "Kokuyo Co., Ltd." in 1961. In May 2011, Kokuyo S&T Co., Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary of Kokuyo, acquired a 50.74% stake in Camlin Ltd. ==See also == * [[Hindustan Pencils]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * {{Official website}} * [https://www.kokuyo.co.jp/ Kokuyo Japan (Japanese)] {{Pen manufacturers}} {{Fountain pen manufacturers}} {{Art materials brands}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Pen manufacturers]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 1931]] [[Category:Multinational joint-venture companies]] [[Category:Indian brands]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1931]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]]
extract:
Kokuyo Camlin Ltd., is an Indian stationery manufacturing company based in Mumbai. The company shares profits with Kokuyo of Japan, which holds around 51% stake in Kokuyo Camlin.
The company sells products related to art materials, writing implements and office goods.
